title: Kenya4Resilience Consortium
summary: Integrated resilience programming connecting community-led peacebuilding, climate-smart livelihoods, natural resource governance and inclusive services across arid and semi-arid communities.
role: Project Coordinator · Climate Resilience & MEAL Lead
contribution: Coordinated multi-partner field delivery, community engagement, work planning, monitoring and learning, partner reporting and government liaison. Convened peace and cross-border dialogues, supported voluntary disarmament, strengthened farmer-market linkages and used KoboCollect and Power BI to track results.
outcomes: 18 peacebuilding and cross-border dialogue forums with more than 450 participants, including community elders, youth and security actors.
317 weapons surrendered through voluntary disarmament work in Wamba sub-county.
800+ smallholders connected to input suppliers, off-takers and local traders.
Seven health outreaches with Wamba Level IV Hospital and AMREF, reaching approximately 300 households.
Programme learning captured through donor reports, outcome maps and 17 impact stories; communications assets were reused by other county chapters.
note: Figures describe programme-level results associated with the consortium portfolio during the period. They are not presented as outcomes attributable to one individual alone.

title: MSETO Resilience WASH & Food Security
summary: A multi-county resilience programme combining water, sanitation and hygiene, food security, livelihoods and practical inclusion support for schools and vulnerable households.
role: WASH & Livelihoods Project Officer · Special Schools Project Officer
contribution: Coordinated WASH and livelihood activities, school infrastructure rehabilitation, accessible sanitation and pathways, hygiene supply distribution, field monitoring and stakeholder liaison across several counties.
outcomes: Supported improvements to accessible ablution facilities, latrines, pathways, kitchens and water-harvesting systems.
Coordinated distribution of hygiene materials, bedding, mattresses, water purification supplies and sick-bay items.
Organised child-protection, safeguarding and health-promotion training for more than 3,000 learners, teachers and caregivers.

Supported practical life-skills activities and inclusive services for learners with disabilities, including specialist support at Salvation Army Joytown, Thika High School for the Blind and Variety Village.
note: The KES 267 million figure is the wider programme portfolio value recorded in the CV source, not an individual-managed budget.

title: Healthy Nursery Children Project
org: The Salvation Army Kenya East Territory
summary: A child-centred programme design bringing together mobile health outreach, nutrition, safe learning environments, WASH access and child-rights support for nursery schools and children’s homes.
contribution: The Drive source proposal sets out the problem analysis, target groups, outcomes, mobile outreach model, school health and nutrition approach, WASH improvements, child safety and rights activities, and monitoring arrangements.
outcomes: Target group: approximately 1,050 children, 45 teachers, 90 support staff and 140 parents or caregivers.
Five intended outcome areas: child health and nutrition; parent and teacher capacity; WASH access; child rights and protection; and monitoring and evaluation.
Proposed mobile outreach partnerships with county health services, with growth monitoring, vaccination follow-up, referrals and health education.
School-level improvements included safer facilities, water access, sanitation and handwashing.
note: This case study presents the project proposal and its planned targets. Targets should not be read as verified completion figures.

title: Jibu Economic Empowerment Project (JEEP)
org: The Salvation Army Kenya East Territory · CP21-KYE.1148
summary: An integrated three-year programme proposal linking village savings and loan associations, resilient value chains and household nutrition across four counties in Eastern Kenya.
role: Proposal development · Budget and programme narrative integration
contribution: Developed a comprehensive project narrative from the harmonised HIVE budget workbook, aligning context analysis, outcomes, activities, staffing, delivery targets and budget figures with the Salvation Army proposal structure.
outcomes: Geographic focus: Machakos, Makueni, Kitui and Embu counties, with a Learning and Research Centre in Thika and a satellite demonstration site at Karurumo Youth Polytechnic.

Planned reach includes 30 VSLA groups with about 700 members trained, 300 lead farmers and VSLA leaders receiving enterprise and value-chain training, and 600 households receiving kitchen-garden starter inputs.
Three programme outcomes: improved access to finance and social capital; improved household income and resilience; and better access to balanced diets through kitchen gardens and agro-ecology.
Proposal cost and funding allocations were reconciled to the harmonised budget workbook.
note: This is a proposal-stage design. The figures above are planned targets and budget estimates, not reported implementation results.

title: Community Relations & Environmental Compliance
org: TerraOre Mineral Resources Ltd · Ikolomani, Kakamega County
summary: Community engagement and environmental compliance support for a minerals processing project, including stakeholder mapping and a phased household relocation process.
contribution: Led community engagement from early consultation to project start-up, mapped affected households and local stakeholders, supported relocation appraisal and compensation coordination, and followed up environmental licence conditions.
outcomes: Coordinated the relocation and compensation process for seven affected households through cash payments and new homes on purchased, titled land.
Supported the NEMA Environmental Impact Assessment process for the Molowa plant (licence NEMA/EIA/PSL/32674).
Maintained working relationships with host community members, local leaders and government offices.
Supported company registration with the Ministry of Mining and represented a youth cooperative at a sector stakeholder workshop.
note: Household relocation and compensation are described at programme level; individual household identities and personal details are intentionally not published.

title: Pharmacy Operations & Supply Systems
summary: Building practical operating systems for a community pharmacy, with attention to procurement, stock visibility, supplier comparison and accountable day-to-day operations.
contribution: Supported the pharmacy set-up, premises and interior planning, procurement and stock controls, supplier quotation comparison, expiry tracking, logistics, payroll administration and regulatory documentation.
outcomes: Established inventory controls across more than 800 product lines, tracking stock levels, expiry dates and stock-outs.
Coordinated procurement from licensed distributors and compared supplier quotations to support purchasing decisions.
Supported medicine supply to county government hospitals and a church-organised health outreach.
Administered operating systems, payroll, banking processes and KRA documentation.
note: This is a cross-sector operations example demonstrating transferable skills in controls, procurement, logistics and service delivery.
